entries.content: Analysis of Gnostic Patterns (Moderate Research Depth) - Central themes in gnostic texts: - Dualism: a belief that the material world is inherently evil and spirit is good - Knowledge as salvation: acquiring secret, spiritual knowledge can lead to redemption - Myth of Sophia: Sophia, a divine figure, produces imperfect offspring, causing chaos in the universe - Fallen Archons: powerful entities that rule over the material world and keep humanity ignorant - Redeemer figures: enlightened beings who bring knowledge to help humanity escape the material world - Key gnostic texts: - Nag Hammadi Library (includes: The Gospel of Thomas, The Gospel of Philip, The Hypostasis of the Archons, and The Apocryphon of John) - Pistis Sophia - The Secret Book of John - The Acts of Peter and the Twelve Apostles - The Treatises on the Resurrection - Influence on modern culture: - Ideas about dualism, secret knowledge, and redemption have influenced various religious movements, philosophies, and spiritual
